topic: Mobile Equipment Operations (Dozer, Breaker, Loader, Refuelling)
title: Mobile Equipment Operations (Dozer, Breaker, Loader, Refuelling)
body: ADW runs a mixed fleet — dozers, hydraulic breakers, wheel loaders, water pumps, LVs — all working close to haul roads, the ROM pad, and dump edges. Small procedural lapses on this equipment (wrong gear, no three-point mounting, engine running at the fuel bay) turn into GET damage, dropped-object injuries, or fire incidents fast. Refuelling alone already has four logged incidents from missing supervision.
keyPoints: **Dozer:** 1st gear forward, 2nd gear reverse, full stop before changing direction. Steer with blade tilt cylinders, not steering clutches, once the blade is loaded — saves the undercarriage and cuts uneven GET wear.
**Hydraulic rock breaker:** windscreen guard fitted, lights and amber strobe on at all times, seatbelt on. It's there to clear oversize at the crusher feed in place — not a general-purpose hammer.
**Boarding any machine:** three points of contact, always — two hands one foot, or two feet one hand. Face the machine, never jump, nothing carried in the hands (lanyard or hoist instead).

**Refuelling:** engine off, ignition off, key removed, no phones or open flame in the zone, spill kit staged. This is the exact failure mode behind NCR 25-037, the gas-station near-miss, the MG-85 wall strike, and the June diesel overflow — same missing-supervision pattern every time.
**Parking:** drive-through by default, 50 m clear of the loader turning circle at the ROM pad, never behind operating equipment.
apply: With the go-line fuel bay still mid-upgrade (second dispensing point, extra tank pushed to next year), expect trucks queuing tighter at the pump — walk the refuelling zone once this shift and confirm engines are actually off and the spotter/attendant setup is being followed, not just assumed.
